subject: English
central_question: How can resilience, empathy, inclusion, and purposeful communication help people transform challenges into a world of limitless possibilities?
in_scope_units: Paralympics – Reflect and Respond through Sheetal Devi's image and prior knowledge about the Games
Paralympics – Reading for Meaning through the interview with Dr. Deepa Malik
Paralympics – Check Your Understanding using a fact table, fact-opinion, and cause-effect relationships
Paralympics – Critical Reflection on transformation, stereotypes, tone, title, advocacy, and life lessons
Paralympics – Vocabulary and Structures in Context covering phrases, movement words, modal auxiliaries, and direct and reported speech
Paralympics – Listen and Respond to a school special-assembly announcement
Paralympics – Speaking Activity using formal and informal sports interviews
Paralympics – Writing Task on notice format and an Inter-school Athletic Meet notice
Paralympics – Learning Beyond the Text on the origin of the Paralympics and a group presentation
Nine Gold Medals – Reflect and Respond on Olympics, Special Olympics, Paralympics, empathy, sympathy, and compassion
Nine Gold Medals – Reading for Appreciation of David Roth's eight-stanza poem
Nine Gold Medals – Check Your Understanding through contextual vocabulary, stanza gist, imagery, alliteration, tone, mood, and message
Nine Gold Medals – Critical Reflection through extract-based and analytical questions
Nine Gold Medals – Vocabulary in Context through collocations and adjective choice
Nine Gold Medals – Listen and Respond to a radio-talk about Patrick Gomes
Nine Gold Medals – Speaking Activity on expressing points of view about Special Olympics
Nine Gold Medals – Writing Task on slogans and poster design
Nine Gold Medals – Learning Beyond the Text on Indian Special Olympics achievers and an Olympics infographic
banned_topics: Detailed medical treatment of spine tumours beyond the diagnosis, surgery, paralysis, and wheelchair outcome stated in the interview
Biographies or achievements of athletes not named in the chapter, except as student research topics rather than taught facts
Detailed rules, classifications, scoring systems, or training methods of individual Paralympic and Special Olympics sports
A complete history of the ancient or modern Olympic movement beyond the facts included in the chapter's infographic
Answers to the listening exercises without using the teacher transcripts referred to on page 268
Unrelated grammar topics beyond modal auxiliaries and the direct-to-reported-speech transformations taught in this unit

known_pitfalls.claim: Dr. Deepa Malik won a gold medal at the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games.
known_pitfalls.correction: She secured the silver medal in the shot-put event at the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games.

known_pitfalls.claim: Dr. Deepa Malik began para-athletics before her surgery.
known_pitfalls.correction: After the surgery and the declaration that she would be wheelchair-bound, she chose to switch from her earlier experience as a swimmer to para-athletics.

known_pitfalls.claim: The interview says physical strength alone helped Dr. Malik overcome her challenges.
known_pitfalls.correction: She says that overcoming underestimation required physical strength, mental resilience, family support, and fortitude.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every statement made by Dr. Malik in the interview is a fact.
known_pitfalls.correction: Some statements are factual, while statements expressing how she felt or interpreted an event are opinions.

known_pitfalls.claim: The eight runners in 'Nine Gold Medals' continued racing and left the fallen athlete behind.
known_pitfalls.correction: They stopped, turned back, helped him to his feet, joined hands, and walked together to the finish line.

known_pitfalls.claim: The nine gold medals reward only athletic speed.
known_pitfalls.correction: The poem presents the medals and standing ovation as recognition of compassion, unity, and collective support.

known_pitfalls.claim: Paralympics and Special Olympics are identical terms.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes the Paralympics as games showcasing athletes with disabilities, while the Special Olympics provides training and competition for children and adults with intellectual disabilities and promotes acceptance and inclusion.

known_pitfalls.claim: Listening-task answers can be completed from the visible questions alone.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that the listening answers depend on the teacher transcripts on page 268, so they should not be invented.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with Check Your Understanding II (1) from the interview to distinguish fact from opinion.
Use Critical Reflection I.1(iv) from the interview to interpret the phrase 'in hindsight' as reflective thinking.
Use Vocabulary and Structures in Context V to convert Dr. Malik's direct speech into reported speech.
Use Nine Gold Medals Check Your Understanding II to arrange the eight stanza gists in sequence.
Use Nine Gold Medals Critical Reflection I.1(v) to explain why the runners' return is the poem's turning point.
Finish with Learning Beyond the Text III to compare the Paralympics and Special Olympics and interpret the infographic.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The unit has no single separately numbered end-of-chapter exercise; its assessable tasks are distributed across Check Your Understanding, Critical Reflection, Vocabulary, Listen and Respond, Speaking Activity, Writing Task, and Learning Beyond the Text on pages 143–168.
